Member web app (Cookbook) + admin SPA — the web-app plan, end to end (#209)

* Member web app + admin SPA consolidation solution plan

Working plan for an orchestrator agent: one SPA stack (React 19, TanStack
Query/Router, shadcn/ui, PWA/offline) for the member app and the admin
rewrite, first-party cookie sessions on the existing invite machinery, a
per-area typed /api surface over the existing throw-free src/ operations,
and the deterministic backend lifts (propose interaction extensions,
recipe-to-grocery expansion, identity-graph substitutions, aisle capture).
Phased for autonomous execution; design source remains the Claude Design
project.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CLdUFxqUguFmpLnLbG668S

* Plan revisions: ETags, build-version skew check, derived to-buy flow

Go-all-the-way conditional requests (weak ETags + 304s on reads, If-Match
on whole-document writes, canonical-id LWW upserts kept If-Match-free so
offline replay never 412s), a build-version header + /api/version endpoint
for skew-triggered update prompts, and W2 reframed: no discrete
plan-to-list expansion — computeToBuy's derivation becomes a first-class
read (virtual menu rows on the grocery view) and both the agent and the
app converge on derive → make cart → substitutions. Playwright wording
hardened to blocking-from-P0. Commits the extracted design bundle at
docs/plans/web-app-design/ for the plan's lifecycle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CLdUFxqUguFmpLnLbG668S

* Plan: prefer Rust-based build tooling, applied broadly

Encodes the tooling selection principle (native/Rust over JS when widely
community-supported, re-evaluated per phase) with current picks: Vite on
the Rolldown core, SWC/Oxc transforms, Tailwind v4 Oxide, Oxlint + Biome
for the new packages; tsc/Vitest/Playwright stay until native successors
are production-stable.

feat(runtime): serve 404/5xx/root-redirect in Hono; drop Traefik plugin

Moves 404, 5xx, and root-redirect responsibilities from Traefik into the
app so the workflow-engine image is self-contained. Collapses the main
IngressRoute to a single catch-all and deletes the inline-response plugin
scaffolding (init container, ConfigMap, vendored tarball).

Global `app.notFound` + `app.onError` in createApp branch on `Accept:
text/html`; sub-apps (`/api`, `/trigger`, `/dashboard`) install the same
shared factory because Hono sub-apps mounted via `app.use` don't bubble
their 404s to the parent. New `error.html` mirrors `404.html` (linked
stylesheet, plain link, CSP-clean); `error.css` folded into
`workflow-engine.css` under `body.error-page` scoping.

OpenSpec: self-contained-app-image. 822/822 tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(ui): prepare dashboard + trigger for strict CSP

Swap alpinejs/dist/cdn.min.js -> @alpinejs/csp. Register every Alpine
component via Alpine.data(...) so HTML expressions reduce to bare
identifiers and single method calls. Move multi-statement bodies and
global access (clearTimeout, JSON.parse, navigator.clipboard) into
component methods, where the CSP evaluator does not reach. Convert
:style bindings to object form so Alpine sets styles via
setProperty (CSP-safe) instead of attribute writes (blocked).

Extract inline <style> blocks from trigger/page.ts and static/404.html
into external stylesheets. Replace static style="" with classes and
dynamic color attrs with data-color selectors in workflow-engine.css.

Replace ontoggle/onclick inline handlers on the trigger page with
addEventListener wiring in trigger-forms.js, passing the event name
via data-event-type on the submit button.

New html-invariants.test.ts locks in CSP-safe rendering: no inline
<script>/<style>/on*=/style= across every HTML surface, every x-data
is a bare identifier, every :style is object form.

No response-header changes yet; those land in the follow-up once the
UI is confirmed CSP-ready. Part of openspec change add-security-headers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: add custom 404/5xx error pages and reorganize Traefik routing

Replace per-route opt-in auth model with explicit whitelists (auth,
no-auth, app-auth) and a deny-by-default catch-all. Unknown paths now
show a styled 404 page served from the app's static assets. 5xx errors
are handled via a Traefik self-loopback using the traefik_inline_response
plugin on an internal HTTP entrypoint, so the error page renders even
when the app is erroring.

New routes: /livez (public), /api/* (app-auth), /* catch-all (404).
New middlewares: not-found (404), server-error (5xx), inline-error (plugin).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

anchor_commit_observation.message:
feat(trivia): reversible invalidation + state-complete card projection

Invalidating a trivia question was a one-way door: no tool cleared `invalidated`, so a prediction posted in advance and invalidated at reveal (result not yet known) could only be recovered by hand-editing questions.json.

- settle_question gains a `reopen` verb (inverse of invalidate): clears invalidated/invalidatedReason, returns a keyless prediction to pending, keeps a settled key, and never touches processedAt/answerLocked/answer rows. Its description drops the never-existent skip/skipped references.
- refresh_question_cards (renamed from update_answers_block) projects whichever state the record is in — invalidated / revealed (keyed AND processedAt) / locked / live — reusing the single live-render path extracted as roster.resolveLiveOrLockedCard. The results footer is never painted while processedAt is unset, closing an answer leak.
- compute_answers reprocess refuses targets with no processedAt (per-id error), so a live question can no longer be stamped processed and dropped from the pending reveal.
- update_question renamed to set_reveal_narrative (it only ever wrote revealBlocks).
- Reveal prompt notes invalidation is reversible; the admin runbook documents the reopen -> repaint -> settle -> reprocess -> repaint recovery.

Spec deltas archived and main specs synced.

**Goal:** Add the Lambda Function URL runtime shell, event/request/response adapters, and backend CDK wiring. No chat domain logic; only transport.

3. **TRIANGULATE** — Add null-body response test (falls back to `arrayBuffer()`), add stream error handling test (logs and ends stream safely).

### PR 2 — Cognito Access-Token Owner Adapter

**Goal:** Add a Lambda-specific `getOwner` adapter that verifies `Authorization: Bearer <Cognito access token>` and maps `sub` to `OwnerContext`.

- `src/lib/auth/lambda-owner.ts`
- `src/lib/auth/lambda-owner.test.ts`

**TDD Evidence Required**

1. **RED** — Write `lambda-owner.test.ts` with a Cognito JWKS mock:
   - Missing header → throws `AuthRequiredError`.

   - Wrong issuer → throws `AuthRequiredError`.
   - Wrong client/audience → throws `AuthRequiredError`.
   - Wrong `token_use` (e.g., `id`) → throws `AuthRequiredError`.

feat(artifacts): serve PDFs via Lambda-signed S3 URLs

Move PDF view/download out of the Next.js SSR route and into the
chat-streaming Lambda Function URL, which already owns the S3 write
side. The Lambda authenticates the Cognito Bearer token, verifies
thread ownership and artifact readiness, then returns a freshly
presigned GET URL (5 min TTL) so the browser fetches bytes directly
from S3.

Why
- SSR route required CHAT_ATTACHMENTS_S3_BUCKET and s3:GetObject on
  the Amplify-managed Hosting compute role; neither were configured,
  so every View/Download returned a 0-byte response.
- Presigning on-demand from the Lambda preserves 'users can view and
  download any time' because the persisted downloadUrl points to the
  stable Lambda endpoint, not to an expiring URL.

Changes
- Add presign(...) to ArtifactPdfStorage / S3ArtifactPdfStorage using
  @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner with ResponseContentDisposition.
- Add a GET branch + artifact-presign module to the Lambda handler.
- pdfDownloadUrl now emits Lambda URL with threadId/kind query params.
- ArtifactToolCard buttons fetch the presigned URL with the Cognito
  Bearer token, then window.open the result.
- Delete /api/threads/[threadId]/artifacts/[kind]/[format] route and
  its 11 tests; replace with unit tests on the new module + client
  helper.
feat: implement H2O Allegiant Discovery Agent v3 with enhanced artifact storage, discovery skills, and AI SDK integration.
Restore Function URL preflight CORS
Fix Lambda streaming CORS
Port chat streaming to Lambda Function URL

## Phase 1 amendment — active banner-grab phase in sweep service

This amendment adds an opt-in active banner-grab phase to the
existing **sweep service** (`go/pkg/scan/`, NOT the SNMP/API-focused
mapper at `go/pkg/mapper/`). The phase runs after the SYN half-open
scanner identifies live `(host, port)` pairs and emits
`BannerObservation` records that the agent forwards to netprobe in
bounded batches over a new `MatchBanners` IPC method. Netprobe matches
the supplied observations against the §32 Recog / Satori corpora and
returns labels; the agent emits or forwards the resulting
`FingerprintEvent`s. No corpus duplication, no shared Rust/Go crate, no
cgo. Banner grab is a streaming enrichment pipeline over SYN-confirmed
open ports, not a second in-memory scanner; preserve the SYN half-open
scanner's large-inventory latency profile while allowing exhaustive
active probing when operators choose that trade-off. HTTPS/TLS evidence
stays in the passive TLS/SSL fingerprint pipeline rather than active
HTTPS decryption. See `design.md` D16 for the architectural rationale.

Simplify electron bootstrap derived state (#18)

* feat(electron): simplify bootstrap to derived state (LaunchSource V2)

Implements OpenSpec change `simplify-electron-bootstrap-derived-state`.
Replaces stored startup decisions (`mode.json`, `isFirstRun`,
`decideStartupAction`) with derived-on-launch capability probes plus an
explicit `DASHBOARD_STARTER` env var stamped on every server spawn.

New capabilities
- electron-launch-source: discriminated `LaunchSource` resolver across
  attach / devMonorepo / piExtension / npmGlobal / extracted, with
  `DASHBOARD_PREFER_SOURCE` override.
- electron-bundle-extract: version-marker-driven extraction of
  `~/.pi-dashboard/`, config migration to `~/.pi/dashboard/migrate/<ts>/`,
  and the `node|node-pending|node-old` survive-extract whitelist.
- dashboard-starter-identity: `DASHBOARD_STARTER` env contract,
  `/api/health.starter` + `/api/health.pid` exposure, lifecycle ownership
  rule "only the starter, with pid match, may stop on quit".
- installable-list: `~/.pi/dashboard/installable.json` schema +
  server-side reconcile in `bootstrap-install-from-list.ts` (no-op when
  file absent).

Removed
- first-run-wizard capability: `mode.json`, `isFirstRun`,
  `decideStartupAction`, `runPowerUserManagedInstall` deletions deferred
  to a follow-up change once `LAUNCH_SOURCE_V2=false` legacy path is
  retired.
- NSIS installer + portable .exe: ZIP is now the sole Windows
  distribution (cross-platform reproducible from Docker).

Phase C bring-up fixes (Windows ZIP)
- launch-source.ts: extract from `<resourcesPath>/server`, not bare
  `resourcesPath` (top-level contains app.asar, recursive cpSync ENOTDIRs
  on opendir).
- launch-source.ts: extraction error log now includes
  code/syscall/path/message so failing entry is identifiable.
- docker-make.sh: replace every workspace symlink under
  `node_modules/@blackbelt-technology/*`, not a hardcoded subset
  (previously missed `dashboard-plugin-runtime`, dangling symlink tripped
  ENOTDIR on Windows first-launch cpSync).
- build-windows-zip.sh: anonymous Docker volume on
  `/build/packages/electron/out` to dodge Docker Desktop FUSE/VirtioFS
  EACCES on read-after-write; `--platform linux/amd64` pinned on build
  and run; `--name` + `docker cp` artifact extraction.

Supersedes
- electron-startup-splash (archived)
- electron-wizard-smart-detection (archived)

* test(electron): real-fs smoke for LaunchSource V2 + fix bootstrap regressions

Adds a tiered real-fs smoke test for the `extracted` source path that
catches the class of bugs unit tests can't see (pure mocks miss
real-fs/npm/spawn behavior). Fixes three production regressions
the smoke test surfaced.

New test file
- packages/electron/src/lib/__tests__/launch-source.smoke.test.ts
  - Tier A (always when bundle present, ~2s): real `extractBundle` over
    the host's `resources/server/`; pins layout + cliPath presence + no
    absolute symlinks.
  - Tier B (when offline cache + bundled node also present, ~30s):
    `selectLaunchSource({ preferOverride: "extracted" })` end-to-end;
    pins pi-coding-agent install, cliPath survival, jiti resolution.
  - Tier C (when host node-pty prebuild matches, ~10s): real `node
    --import <jiti> <cliPath>` spawn; pins /api/health = starter:Electron.
  - Skips cleanly with explicit reasons when prerequisites absent;
    fresh-clone friendly.

Production fixes uncovered by the smoke test

1. cpSync rewrites relative symlinks as absolute paths (Node quirk)
   - Repro: `fs.cpSync(src, dst, { recursive: true, dereference: false })`
     on a relative symlink writes an absolute path pointing at the build
     host's source tree. Users see a broken cliPath after extraction.
   - Fix: bundle-server.mjs materializes every workspace symlink under
     `@blackbelt-technology/*` before forge packs the bundle. Mirrors

* openspec: propose fix-electron-extracted-jiti-and-stdio-capture

install:

1. selectLaunchSource() returns kind=extracted with cliPath whose tree
   is degraded (jiti missing). spawnFromSource() then FATALs because
   resolveJitiFromAnchor returns null and the fallback resolveJitiImport
   uses process.argv[1] = electron.exe which cannot resolve jiti.
   Root: needsExtraction only checks .version marker, not tree health.

   blinding diagnostics. server/cli.ts already does this correctly with
   raw spawn(); spawnDetached is the outlier.

- extractedSourceIsHealthy(cliPath) pure helper + wiring to force
  re-extract when marker matches but tree is degraded.
- spawnDetached.logFd routes to both stdout and stderr.

* build(electron): pin appdmg + fail fast on incompatible Node versions

When building the macOS DMG locally on Node 25, the Electron build failed
deep inside electron-forge with 'Cannot find module appdmg'. Two contributing
gaps:

  1. `appdmg` is an *optional* transitive dep of `electron-installer-dmg`
     (used by `@electron-forge/maker-dmg`). On certain npm runs it gets
     skipped silently, leaving DMG building broken with no upfront signal.

  2. `appdmg` itself depends on `macos-alias`, a native module that does
     not compile on Node 25 (V8 internal API changes). Today this surfaces
     only when the user runs `npm run electron:build` — too late and too
     opaque.

Fixes:

  - Add `appdmg` to root `optionalDependencies` so npm always attempts
    the install rather than skipping it as a deep transitive optional.
  - Add root `engines.node` (`>=22.12.0 <25`) — `<25` excludes the
    macos-alias-incompatible Node 25 line. Documented prerequisite in
    docs/faq.md is already "Node.js 22.12+", so this codifies it.
  - Add `.npmrc` with `engine-strict=true` so a fresh `npm install` on
    Node 25 fails fast with EBADENGINE rather than silently skipping
    optional `appdmg` and erroring at `electron-forge make` time.

Verified:

  - Node 22.22.2: `npm install` succeeds, `node_modules/appdmg/` present.
  - Node 25.8.1: `npm install --dry-run` errors with `EBADENGINE` — fail fast.

Discovered while running the local Intel macOS DMG build for the
`doctor-rich-output` change. Build now completes cleanly to
`packages/electron/out/make/PI-Dashboard-darwin-x64-0.4.6.dmg` (156 MB).

commits.message:
refactor(whisper): remove whisper_manager.py (task 2.4)

The subprocess lifecycle manager is replaced by in-process WhisperModel loading
in the FastAPI lifespan (task 2.2). All callers were rewired in tasks 2.1/2.2.

grep -r whisper_manager app/ tests/ → no matches.
Targeted suite (test_main, test_config, test_whisper, test_punctuation,
test_files) passes 62/62; test_api.py is v1-style and rewritten in task 3.x.

refactor(whisper): make server lifecycle async and introduce typed errors

Replace runtime string-matching error detection with dedicated exception
classes (WhisperServerError, WhisperConnectError, WhisperTimeoutError).
Convert whisper_manager.stop() and _kill_pid() to async, eliminating
blocking time.sleep() calls. Reuse a single health-check result in
lifespan startup to avoid a redundant HTTP call. Reuse an httpx.AsyncClient
across polling iterations in _wait_for_ready() for connection efficiency.
Fix file-handle leak in _do_transcribe by opening the WAV file in a
context manager.

fix(transcribe,whisper_manager): handle audio/x-m4a and external whisper-server processes

- Add "audio/x-m4a" MIME type mapping to the raw transcription endpoint
  so iOS devices sending that content-type receive correct file extension
- Refactor WhisperServerManager.is_running to an equivalent but cleaner form
- Add _find_external_pid() to detect whisper-server processes started
  outside the manager (e.g. via `make dev`) using lsof
- Add _kill_pid() to gracefully terminate external PIDs with SIGTERM/SIGKILL fallback
- Update stop() to handle both managed and externally started processes;
  after stopping a managed process it checks for and kills any external one
- Update restart() docstring to reflect the expanded scope

feat(whisper): add auto-restart process manager for whisper-server

Introduce WhisperServerManager to manage the whisper-server process
lifecycle (start, stop, restart) from within the FastAPI application.

When WHISPER_AUTO_RESTART is enabled, the transcription client
automatically restarts the whisper-server on connection or server
errors and retries the request up to WHISPER_MAX_RETRIES times.
A restart lock prevents concurrent restart races when multiple
requests fail simultaneously.

New config options: WHISPER_BINARY_PATH, WHISPER_AUTO_RESTART,
WHISPER_MAX_RETRIES.

anchor_commit_observation.message:
docs(openspec): design-fidelity-ui-primitive-sync change — primitive sync proposal

The v0 design source frequently uses extended shadcn primitive APIs
(CommandDialog with title/description, newer Dialog variants) that
the project-side src/components/ui/ does not implement. Skeleton check
passes, then the next gate dies with a TypeScript build error like
"Property 'title' does not exist on type 'DialogProps'".

This is a contract gap between v0-export/components/ui/ and the
project's primitive layer — not a v0/agent/build bug. Right now the
framework treats them as independent, so any v0-side primitive
customization causes a guaranteed retry cycle.

Artifacts propose adding sync_ui_primitives() to v0_importer.py that
mirrors v0-export/components/ui/**.tsx into src/components/ui/,
overwrites on byte-difference, never deletes, with INFO logging per
sync. Specs cover: ui-primitive-sync semantics, design-fidelity gate
behaviour, v0-design-import CLI plumbing.

No implementation in this commit — artifacts only.

  cljs-bermuda-test:
